English Proficiency
English Proficiency Requirement
Graduate students must demonstrate a level of oral proficiency in the English language sufficient to participate successfully in the various activities that comprise a graduate education, including classwork, research, research presentations, group meetings, project teamwork, and teaching undergraduates.
Please refer to our English Language Proficiency Policy for full details.
Who Needs to Submit Scores
If your primary language is not English, you must meet English language proficiency requirements and may be required to submit TOEFL, IELTS, or DET test scores.
We accept scores from the following internationally recognized English language proficiency tests:
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL)
International English Language Testing System (IELTS)
Duolingo English Test (DET)
The Graduate School does not have a minimum score requirement. Please review the Fields of Study page for department specific requirements. In accordance with our English Language Proficiency policy, graduate students must demonstrate a level of oral proficiency in the English language sufficient to participate successfully in all various activities that comprise graduate education. Based on your complete application file, including scores on your English language exams, if you are offered admission and accept our offer, you may be required to take an English language proficiency assessment by our McGraw Center for Teaching and Learning. If you were to not pass that test, you would be placed in English language classes concurrently with the degree program classes.
Send test scores no later than three weeks before the degree program application deadline to ensure receipt of the official score report. Test scores received after the deadline will still be matched to your application; however, no offers of admission will be made if required scores are not in the application. You do not need to wait on test scores to submit your application. If your application is on file when scores are received, we will match them to your application within seven business days.
Exemptions from Testing
The following applicants are not required to submit English language test scores. All other applicants must submit valid TOEFL, IELTS or DET scores:
Applicants whose primary language is English. Primary language is defined as the language that someone communicates in most frequently and in most situations when speaking, reading, and writing.
Applicants whose undergraduate instruction is entirely in English as certified by the institution and for whom the degree will be awarded prior to anticipated enrollment at Princeton.
Applicants whose graduate study was on a full-time basis for at least two academic years where instruction was entirely in English as certified by the institution. Please note that this requirement must be fully met at the time the application opens to qualify for the exemption.
English Language Tests
TOEFL
Educational Testing Service (ETS) administers the TOEFL internet-based test. The Graduate School accepts the TOEFL iBT taken either in test centers or at home. Beginning January 21, 2026, ETS introduced a new TOEFL iBT scoring scale (1-6). Applicants may submit TOEFL scores reported on either the new 1-6 scale or the previous 0-120 scale, and both formats will be accepted for admission review. For more information contact ETS.

Duolingo English Test (DET)
Duolingo administers DET which is entirely computer-based and can be taken from any location with an internet connection.

Additional Testing Upon Enrollment
If your scores are as follows you will be required to take an English language proficiency assessment upon enrollment regardless of if you qualified for an exemption:
TOEFL (Speaking) of lower than 5.5 (on 1-6 scale) or 27 (on 0-120 scale)
IELTS (Speaking) of lower than 8.0
DET (Conversation) of lower than 125
Score Validity and Review
Only valid, unexpired test scores will be considered.
Beginning with Fall 2026 admission, test scores will only be considered if they remain valid as of the date the application opens (September 15). Scores that expire before the application opening date—even if submitted earlier—will not be accepted.
Once submitted, scores cannot be removed or excluded from the review process.
All submitted scores are subject to review by the Graduate School.
